A pump plant as the reference example
Ownership, integration and the Azure architecture

takeaways: Write traceability requirements backward from the recall and containment decisions your quality team must be able to defend.
Record material contributions as explicit relationships captured at the moment of use, with identities, quantities and evidence sources, instead of copying planned bills of materials.
Cloud services such as Azure and Microsoft Fabric can carry and analyze the records, but owners, tested event contracts, mock recalls and human approval decide whether the evidence holds.
hook: When a supplier reports a suspect batch, many manufacturers cannot prove which products actually contain it. This episode is for quality managers, MES and ERP owners and manufacturing IT teams who need traceability that holds up in recalls and audits. You will learn how to design identities, genealogy records, integrations and investigations that support defensible decisions.
